setting: A student is talking to her academic advisor about registering for a class.
narrator_intro: Listen to a conversation between a student and her academic advisor.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Professor Hayes, do you have a minute? I wanted to ask about the Statistics course for next semester.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Of course, Melissa. Come on in. What's the issue?

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Well, I checked the schedule, and Statistics 210 is only offered at eight in the morning, three days a week. I work at the campus library until nine most mornings.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: I see. Unfortunately, that's the only section this term, since Dr. Alvarez is on sabbatical. But there is an online version, Statistics 210E. Same content, same credit.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: I didn't even know that existed. Is it just as demanding as the regular class?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: It is, actually a bit more, since you'll need to keep up with weekly deadlines on your own rather than having class discussions to remind you. But if your schedule is tight, it might be the better option.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: That sounds manageable. Could I switch my registration to that section today?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Sure, I can do that right now. Just be aware that the add period for online sections closes this Friday, so you won't be able to switch back easily after that.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: That's fine. My work schedule isn't changing anytime soon, so the online option makes more sense for me.

narrator_outro: Now get ready to answer the questions.

questions.narrator_text: What are the speakers mainly discussing?

options.A: The woman's poor grades in a statistics class
options.B: A scheduling conflict and an alternative course option
options.C: The requirements to become a teaching assistant

questions.explanation: The woman explains she cannot attend the class due to a work conflict, and the advisor proposes the online section as a solution.

questions.narrator_text: Why can't the woman take the regular section of the course?

options.B: It conflicts with her work schedule
options.C: It is not offered this semester
options.D: She has not completed the prerequisite

questions.explanation: She states she works until nine most mornings, which conflicts with the 8 a.m. class time.

questions.narrator_text: According to the advisor, what is different about the online section?

options.B: It requires more independent time management
options.C: It is taught by a different, less experienced instructor

questions.explanation: The advisor says the online course is a bit more demanding because students must keep up with deadlines without in-class reminders.

questions.narrator_text: What can be inferred about the woman's decision?

options.A: She is unsure whether she will stay in the course
options.B: She plans to quit her job to attend the regular class
options.C: She is confident the online format fits her situation
options.D: She will wait until next semester to decide

questions.explanation: She agrees to switch immediately and explains that her work schedule isn't changing, showing confidence in her decision.
